rows.en: The coals aren't going to light themselves.
rows.draft: Mashala ha a na ho itukisa ka bo 'ona.
rows.reason: itukisa looks like itokisa (get ready / arrange oneself), not 'light'; fire catching is ho tuka. The nudge to get on with the braai is otherwise fine.
rows.rewrite: Mashala ha a na ho tuka ka bo 'ona.

rows.en: Absolutely beautiful out there.
rows.draft: Ho motle haholo kantle.
rows.reason: motle describes a person; for weather the natives use hotle (the pack's own wrong-register row).
rows.rewrite: Ho hotle haholo kantle.

rows.en: Beach or braai? Yes.
rows.draft: Lebopo kapa braai? E.
rows.reason: Short either/or with a flat 'E' for the answer, same deadpan as the English; lebopo and braai both natural.

rows.en: Fog so thick it has opinions.
rows.draft: Moholi o mokoto haholo o na le maikutlo.
rows.reason: mokoto is not a word I can vouch for as 'thick' for fog (natives would say teteaneng), and moholi is the Lesotho spelling of mohodi.
rows.rewrite: Mohodi o teteaneng hoo o nang le maikutlo.

rows.en: Even the hadedas sound happy.
rows.draft: Esita le dinonyana di utloahala li thabile.
rows.reason: Concord slip: dinonyana takes di, not li, so 'di utloahala li thabile' mixes the two. Plain 'dinonyana' for hadedas is what the natives already kept.
rows.rewrite: Esita le dinonyana di utloahala di thabile.

rows.en: Overcast but we'll survive.
rows.draft: Ho na le maru empa re tla phela.
rows.reason: 'Ho na le maru' is the form the natives themselves used, and 'empa re tla phela' is a natural shrug.

rows.en: Three pairs of socks and still not enough.
rows.draft: Lipara tse tharo tsa dikausu empa ha li ea lekana.
rows.reason: Plain, natural complaint with the right dry understatement; lipara/ha li ea lekana is Lesotho spelling only, and the natives let such spelling stand.

rows.en: Warm one coming, give or take a few degrees.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le futhumetseng le tla, mohlomong.
rows.reason: The English is sure a warm day is coming and only unsure of the degrees; 'mohlomong' puts the doubt on the warm day itself, so the meaning shifts and the 'give or take' wit goes.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le futhumetseng le a tla. Mocheso o ka fapana hanyane.

rows.en: Windows closed, kettle on, and wait.
rows.draft: Lifensetere li koetsoe, ketlele e butsoe, ema.
rows.reason: 'ketlele e butsoe' means the kettle is opened; 'kettle on' is belisa ketlele (the natives' word). 'Ema' alone is also thinner than the English 'and wait'.
rows.rewrite: Koala difensetere, belisa ketlele, mme u lule u emetse.

rows.en: The commute just became a team sport.
rows.draft: Leeto le fetohile papali ea sehlopha.
rows.reason: 'Leeto' is a journey, not the daily commute, and the 'just' is lost; a speaker would name the trip to work.
rows.rewrite: Leeto la ho ea mosebetsing le sa tswa fetoha papali ea sehlopha.

rows.en: The sky just went full Carte Blanche.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le fetohile Carte Blanche ka botlalo.
rows.reason: Carte Blanche stays as the SA TV reference, sentence is natural, and it matches the kept 'le hloka Carte Blanche' line.

rows.en: The fog ate the neighbourhood.
rows.draft: Moholi o jele tikoloho.
rows.reason: 'Tikoloho' is 'the environment', a textbook word; a speaker would say the area where we live. Also moholi is the Lesotho spelling of mohodi.
rows.rewrite: Mohodi o jele sebaka sa heso.

rows.en: The car's heater is the most important relationship in your life right now.
rows.draft: Heater ya koloi ke relationship ya bohlokwa ka ho fetisisa bophelong ba hao hona jwale.
rows.reason: Heater and relationship left in English the way the natives code-switch (cf. the kept 'Cold ya mofuta...'); the heater-as-relationship joke carries.

rows.en: Everything looks 4K today. The sky's in ultra mode.
rows.draft: Tsohle li shebahala 4K kajeno. Lehodimo le ultra mode.
rows.reason: Same code-switched pattern as the kept 'Lehodimo le dramatic...' and 'soundtrack' lines; 4K and ultra mode read as urban Sesotho.

rows.en: Weather's being more indecisive than you at Spur.
rows.draft: Leholimo ha le tsebe ho iketsa joalo ka uena Spur.
rows.reason: 'Ha le tsebe ho iketsa joalo ka uena' has no 'indecisive' and no 'more than'; it reads as 'doesn't know how to act like you', and Spur has no ho. The joke is gone.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo ha le tsebe ho etsa qeto ho feta uena ho Spur.

rows.en: Nothing to see here. Literally.
rows.draft: Ha ho letho leo ho le bonoang mona. Ka nnete.
rows.reason: 'Letho leo ho le bonoang' is stiff and awkward; a speaker says 'ha ho letho le bonahalang' for nothing to see.
rows.rewrite: Ha ho letho le bonahalang mona. Ka nnete.

rows.en: Probably a scorcher. A hat's not a bad idea.
rows.draft: Mohlomong letsatsi le chesang. Katiba hase mohopolo o mobe.
rows.reason: Natural hedge plus the understated 'katiba ha se mohopolo o mobe', same dry turn as the English; katiba is the word the natives use.

rows.en: Stay safe. The sky is making a point.
rows.draft: Lula u bolokehile. Lehodimo le etsa ntlha.
rows.reason: 'Etsa ntlha' is a calque of 'make a point'; it does not read as the sky emphasising something. 'Lula u bolokehile' is fine.
rows.rewrite: Lula u bolokehile. Lehodimo le bua ka matla.

rows.en: The couch has made a compelling case for staying.
rows.draft: Sofa e entsoe nyeoe e matla ea ho dula.
rows.reason: 'Sofa e entsoe nyeoe' is passive (a case was made for the sofa), and nyeoe is a court case; the couch should be the one with the reasons.
rows.rewrite: Sofa e na le mabaka a matla a hore u dule ka hare.

rows.en: Perfect conditions for losing your dignity.
rows.draft: Maemo a phethahetseng a ho lahleheloa ke seriti.
rows.reason: 'Maemo a phethahetseng' with 'ho lahleheloa ke seriti' is correct and the formal-sounding tone gives the dry joke; seriti is the right word for dignity.

rows.en: Quiet out there. Almost suspicious.
rows.draft: Ho kgutsitse kantle. E batla ho belaela.
rows.reason: 'E batla ho belaela' has a stray 'E' and says it almost doubts, rather than looks suspicious; the natives' own form is 'shebahala a belaela'.
rows.rewrite: Ho kgutsitse kantle. Ho batla ho shebahala ho belaela.

rows.en: Don't even think about driving somewhere.
rows.draft: Se ke oa nahana ho otlela kae kapa kae.
rows.reason: Natural prohibitive ('se ke oa nahana'), and 'ho otlela' is the driving verb the native corpus uses; the 'even' is lost, so it reads as a plain warning.

rows.en: Table Mountain? What Table Mountain?
rows.draft: Table Mountain? Table Mountain efe?
rows.reason: Short rhetorical echo; 'efe' is the right 'which' for the loaned mountain name and the deadpan carries.

rows.en: Good enough weather. Not great, not terrible.
rows.draft: Leholimo le lekaneng. Ha le leholo, ha le lebe.
rows.reason: 'ha le leholo' means 'it is not big', not 'not great'; natives used 'ha ho mpe, ha ho motle' for this beat.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le lokile feela. Ha ho mpe, ha ho hotle haholo.

rows.en: The type of day that makes people text 'lekker dag hey'.
rows.draft: Mofuta oa letsatsi o etsang batho ba romele 'letsatsi le letle hey'.
rows.reason: Missing 'hore' after 'etsang', no word for the message (romela alone is just 'send'), and the Afrikaans 'lekker dag' is translated away, which kills the code-switch the joke runs on.
rows.rewrite: Mofuta wa letsatsi o etsang hore batho ba romelane molaetsa o reng 'lekker dag hey'.

rows.en: Your washing just moved to the neighbour's yard.
rows.draft: Liaparo tsa hao li sa tsoa fallela jareteng ea moahisane.
rows.reason: 'Fallela' (move house to) is exactly right for washing relocating to the neighbour; same shape as the kept trampoline line.

rows.en: The kind of day Joburg pretends it doesn't have until you're standing in it.
rows.draft: Letsatsi la mofuta oo Joburg e iketsang eka ha e na lona, ho fihlela o eme ka hara lona.
rows.reason: 'Iketsa eka' is the natural idiom for pretending and the long two-beat sentence reads fluently; Joburg stays as a place name.

rows.en: Eskom-friendly weather. No solar today.
rows.draft: Leholimo le ratoang ke Eskom. Ha ho solar kajeno.
rows.reason: 'Ha ho solar kajeno' is how people say it, Eskom and solar stay as loans; 'le ratoang ke Eskom' is a little formal but clear.

rows.en: The duvet had the right idea this morning.
rows.draft: Duvet e ne e na le mohopolo o nepahetseng hoseng.
rows.reason: Plain and natural; duvet stays as the loan, 'mohopolo o nepahetseng' is a touch formal but the personified duvet lands.

rows.en: Three hadedas, two crows, one shivering human at the bird feeder.
rows.draft: Hadedas tse tharo, crows tse pedi, human a le mong ya thothomelang ho bird feeder.
rows.reason: Same fault as the CUT 'Frost ho pet bowl' anchor: 'crows', 'human' and 'bird feeder' left in English with Sesotho connectors; 'motho' is the plain word for human and the line reads like glued-in English.
rows.rewrite: Dihadeda tse tharo, dinonyana tse ntsho tse pedi, motho a le mong a thothomelang sebakeng sa ho fepa dinonyana.

rows.en: Days like this is why we put up with the load shedding.
rows.draft: Matsatsi a tjena ke lebaka leo re mametseng load shedding.
rows.reason: 're mametseng' looks like the perfect of 'mamela' (to listen), not 'mamella' (to put up with), so it says 'we listened to load shedding'.
rows.rewrite: Matsatsi a tjena ke ona a etsang hore re mamelle load shedding.

rows.en: Take a moment. Look up. You're welcome.
rows.draft: Nka motsotso. Sheba holimo. Kea leboha.
rows.reason: 'Kea leboha' is 'thank you', so the speaker thanks the reader; the cheeky 'you're welcome' is reversed. 'Nka motsotso' is also a stiff calque of 'take a moment'.
rows.rewrite: Ema hanyane. Sheba hodimo. Ha ho letho.

rows.en: Could go misty. The dew point's flirting with it.
rows.draft: Ho ka ba le mohodi. Ela hloko.
rows.reason: First sentence is natural but 'Ela hloko' replaces the dew-point-flirting joke with a plain warning, so the humour is gone.
rows.rewrite: Ho ka ba le mohodi. Dew point e ntse e o sheba ka lerato.

rows.en: You miss your bed and you've been gone twelve minutes.
rows.draft: O hopola bethe ea hao mme o tsoile metsotso e leshome le metso e 'meli.
rows.reason: 'hopola' is 'remember', not 'miss'; the spelled-out 'metsotso e leshome le metso e meli' is stiff where people use digits ('metsotsoana e 30' in the corpus).
rows.rewrite: O lakatsa bethe ya hao, mme o tswile metsotso e 12 feela.

rows.en: Fog might be rolling in. Keep an eye on the mountain.
rows.draft: Mohodi o ka kena. Sheba thaba.
rows.reason: Short, practical and idiomatic: 'mohodi o ka kena' and 'sheba thaba' are plain and match the corpus register.

rows.en: Marinade in. Phone off. Day starts now.
rows.draft: Kenya marinade. Tima mohala. Letsatsi le qala joale.
rows.reason: Three clipped imperatives like the kept 'Letsetsa metswalle. Fumana nama.'; 'tima mohala' is the natural phrase for phone off and marinade stays as the braai loan.

rows.en: Every loose object in the garden has chosen violence.
rows.draft: Ntho e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe e lokolohileng serapaneng e khethile pefo.
rows.reason: Reads fluently and 'khethile pefo' carries the meme the way 'yoga e sa batleheng' was kept; 'lokolohileng' is a slightly free reading of 'loose' but works.

rows.en: Fire up the Weber. It's the law.
rows.draft: Chesa Weber. Ke molao.
rows.reason: Short imperative plus 'Ke molao' is natural and Weber stays as the brand; 'chesa' is the older spelling of 'tjhesa' but the wording is right.

rows.en: The streetlights are trying their best.
rows.draft: Mabone a seterata a leka ka hohle.
rows.reason: 'leka ka hohle' does not say 'try their best' (hohle is 'everywhere/outside'); the natives' way is 'ka matla' or 'sohle se matla'.
rows.rewrite: Mabone a seterata a leka ka matla a wona.

rows.en: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.
rows.draft: Ho bata ho lekana le soupa. Le soupa ea bobeli.
rows.reason: 'soupa' is a known native correction (errors-observed); the word is 'sopho'. 'Ya bobedi' is the SA form for 'second'.
rows.rewrite: Ho bata ho lekana le sopho. Le sopho ya bobedi.

rows.en: The fog drank the mountain.
rows.draft: Moholi o noele thaba.
rows.reason: Grammatical and the 'drank the mountain' image comes through as a short poetic line; 'moholi' is the older spelling of 'mohodi' but the wording works.

rows.en: If you're inside, you're doing it wrong.
rows.draft: Haeba o ka hare, o etsa phoso.
rows.reason: Direct and natural: 'haeba o ka hare, o etsa phoso' is how a speaker would tease.

rows.en: Kuier weather. Get the people together.
rows.draft: Leholimo la ho kopana. Bokella batho.
rows.reason: Warm and natural; 'bokella batho' and 'leholimo la ho kopana' say get-together weather, though the Afrikaans 'kuier' flavour is not kept.

rows.en: Your suede shoes chose today? Bold.
rows.draft: Lieta tsa hao tsa suede li khethile kajeno? Sebete.
rows.reason: Natural, suede stays as the loan, and 'Sebete' (guts) delivers the dry 'Bold' like the kept 'o le sebete' line.

rows.en: Good day for a walk, bad day for a tan.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le letle la ho tsamaea, le lebe la ho tjhesa.
rows.reason: 'ho tjhesa' is 'to burn / be hot', not 'to tan', so the second half reads as a bad day for burning; people just say the loan 'tan'.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le letle la ho tsamaya, empa le sa loketseng ho tan.

rows.en: Nature just reminded us of the pecking order.
rows.draft: Tlhaho e sa tsoa re hopotsa hore na ke mang ea pele.
rows.reason: 'hore na ke mang ea pele' is 'who is first', which loses the pecking-order sense of who is in charge; a speaker would say who rules.
rows.rewrite: Tlhaho e sa tswa re hopotsa hore ke mang ya laolang.

rows.en: Perfect night to actually see the Milky Way.
rows.draft: Bosiu bo motle ba ho bona Tsela ea Lebese.
rows.reason: 'Tsela ea Lebese' is the banned calque for Milky Way (native term is Molalatladi); 'motle' is the person word and does not agree with bosiu, it should be 'botle'.
rows.rewrite: Bosiu bo botle bakeng sa ho bona Molalatladi ka nnete.

rows.en: Sand in places sand should never be.
rows.draft: Lehlabathe libakeng tseo lehlabathe le sa lokelang ho ba teng.
rows.reason: Understood and keeps the repeated-sand beat, but 'libakeng tseo ... ba teng' is a stiff, translated relative clause (no 'ho tsona'); a speaker would say 'moo'.
rows.rewrite: Lehlabathe moo lehlabathe le sa lokelang ho ba teng.

rows.en: Maluti-frost morning. Lesotho's exporting it for free.
rows.draft: Maluti-frost morning. Lesotho e a e exporta mahala.
rows.reason: 'e a e exporta' forces an English verb into Sesotho where people would say romella; 'Maluti-frost morning' is fine as a code-switched block like 'Karoo morning', but frost itself is serame.
rows.rewrite: Maluti-frost morning. Lesotho e re romella serame ka mahala.

rows.en: Somewhere an estate agent is saying 'lifestyle'.
rows.draft: Mohlomong sebakeng se seng estate agent e re 'lifestyle'.
rows.reason: 'Mohlomong sebakeng se seng' adds a 'perhaps' the English does not have; natives use 'kae-kae' for 'somewhere'. The loans estate agent and lifestyle carry the joke well.
rows.rewrite: Kae-kae estate agent e re 'lifestyle'.

rows.en: The frogs have entered the chat.
rows.draft: Digwagwa di kene puisanong.
rows.reason: 'digwagwa' reads as a Setswana/Sepedi frog word; Sesotho is senqanqane (I am fairly, not fully, sure). 'kene puisanong' works as the group-chat image.
rows.rewrite: Dinqanqane di kene puisanong.

rows.en: Could get gusty. The forecast's a bit loose on this one.
rows.draft: Ho ka ba le moea. Ponelopele e hlephile mona.
rows.reason: 'hlephile' means ashamed/shy, not loose or unsure, so the forecast is accidentally 'shy'; 'moea' is the Lesotho spelling of moya and 'gusty' wants moya o matla.
rows.rewrite: Ho ka ba le moya o matla. Ponelopele ha e na bonnete haholo mona.

rows.en: The aircon remote is now public property. Negotiate.
rows.draft: Remote ea aircon joale ke thepa ea sechaba. Buisana.
rows.reason: Natural code-switching (remote, aircon) and 'thepa ea sechaba' carries 'public property' with the dry imperative; 'Buisana' is singular where a household would say buisanang, a small slip.

rows.en: Lekker koud, but the rugby fields are about to look perfect.
rows.draft: Lekker koud, empa di-rugby fields di se di tlo shebahala perfect.
rows.reason: Too much English forced in: 'di-rugby fields' (mabala a rugby) and 'perfect' (phethahetse) where Sesotho has the word; 'Lekker koud' is correctly kept.
rows.rewrite: Lekker koud, empa mabala a rugby a tla shebahala a phethahetse.

rows.en: This is not what the tourism brochure promised.
rows.draft: Hona ha se seo brosure ea bohahlauli e neng e se tšepisa.
rows.reason: Reads naturally: brosure (as the natives write it), bohahlauli for tourism and 'e neng e se tšepisa' carry the dry disappointment.

rows.en: Wet jeans for the rest of the day. The classic punishment.
rows.draft: Lijinse tse metsi letsatsi lohle. Kotlo ea setso.
rows.reason: 'Kotlo ea setso' uses setso for 'classic' as the natives did; 'letsatsi lohle' is 'all day' not 'rest of the day', a minor shift that does not hurt the joke.

rows.en: Somewhere an umbrella just turned inside out. Moment of silence.
rows.draft: Kae-kae sekhele se sa tsoa reteleha ka hare. Motsotso oa kgutso.
rows.reason: Kae-kae, sekhele (the natives' word) and 'motsotso wa kgutso' are all natural; 'reteleha ka hare' is a little loose for 'inside out' but understood.

rows.en: Thunder's grumbling, hey.
rows.draft: Ledimo le a duma.
rows.reason: 'Ledimo' is an ogre/giant, not thunder (thunder is seaduma/modumo), so the line says the ogre is rumbling; the 'hey' tag is also dropped.
rows.rewrite: Seaduma se a ngongorega.

rows.en: The southeaster's arrived. Uninvited, as usual.
rows.draft: Moea oa boroa o fihlile. O sa mengoa, joalo ka kamehla.
rows.reason: 'Moea oa boroa' is a south wind, not the Southeaster, which SA speakers keep as the English name; the rest ('o sa mengoa, jwalo ka kamehla') is natural.
rows.rewrite: Moya wa Southeaster o fihlile. O sa mengoa, jwalo ka kamehla.

rows.en: A perfectly average sky doing perfectly average things.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le karolelano le etsang lintho tsa karolelano.
rows.reason: Stiff but natural enough and mirrors the natives' own 'ba karolelano'; 'perfectly' is dropped so the deadpan is slightly flatter.

rows.en: Stars out, load shedding can't touch this.
rows.draft: Dinaledi di teng, load shedding e ke ke ea ama sena.
rows.reason: Plain, natural; dinaledi di teng and the kept 'load shedding' match the corpus, and 'e ke ke ea ama' carries 'can't touch'.

rows.en: The potholes are becoming swimming pools.
rows.draft: Mesima e fetoha matamo a ho sesa.
rows.reason: Clear image with the right concords (mesima e fetoha, matamo a ho sesa); 'mesima' (pits) is understood for potholes though masoba is also possible.

rows.en: Grey skies, low conviction.
rows.draft: Leholimo le lerootho, tumelo e tlase.
rows.reason: 'tumelo' is religious faith, so 'low conviction' reads as low faith; the natives' word for resolve is maikemisetso.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le lerootho, maikemisetso a tlase.

rows.en: The neighbourhood cats have taken over.
rows.draft: Dikatse tsa moahisane di nkile taolo.
rows.reason: 'moahisane' is one neighbour, while the English is the neighbourhood cats; 'nka taolo' is natural.
rows.rewrite: Dikatse tsa baahisane di nkile taolo.

rows.en: Tile floors are tonight's villain. Wear something on your feet.
rows.draft: Tile floors ke villain ya bosiu bona. Apara ntho maotong.
rows.reason: 'Apara ntho maotong' is stiff and ungrammatical (ntho e nngwe), and 'tile floors' plus 'villain' leave the noun phrases in English where Sesotho has fatshe la ditaele and bothata.
rows.rewrite: Fatshe la ditaele ke bothata ba bosiu bona. Apara ntho e nngwe maotong.

rows.en: If you can read this, you're too close.
rows.draft: Haeba o ka bala sena, o haufi haholo.
rows.reason: Natural bumper-sticker phrasing: 'Haeba o ka bala sena, o haufi haholo' reads like something a person would say.

rows.en: The fynbos is loving it. You should too.
rows.draft: Fynbos e e rata. Le uena o lokela.
rows.reason: Warm and natural; fynbos kept as the SA word and 'Le uena o lokela' is a natural elliptical 'you should too'.

rows.en: The braai is the social calendar. Show up.
rows.draft: Braai ke khalendara ea boithabiso. Hlaha.
rows.reason: Natural; braai kept, khalendara ea boithabiso lands as the social calendar and 'Hlaha' is a fine short imperative.

rows.en: Your iced coffee melted before you reached the car.
rows.draft: Kofi ea hao ea leqhoa e qhibilihile pele o fihla koloing.
rows.reason: Plain, everyday and carries the melted-before-the-car image; 'kofi ea leqhoa' and 'koloing' read naturally.

rows.en: The neighbours' pool has never looked so tempting.
rows.draft: Pool ea baahisane ha e e-s'o shebahale e khahlisang hakana.
rows.reason: 'ha e e-s'o shebahale' means 'has not yet looked', not 'has never looked'; the time word is off, and 'khahlisang' is more 'pleasing' than 'tempting'.
rows.rewrite: Pool ya baahisane ha e so ke e shebahale e le monate hakana.

rows.en: The world ends two metres past the gate.
rows.draft: Lefatše le qetella limithara tse peli ka mose ho heke.
rows.reason: 'qetella' is 'finish for / finally'; the plain word for the world ending at a point is 'fela'. The image and the gate position are fine.
rows.rewrite: Lefatše le fela dimithara tse peli ka mose ho heke.

rows.en: Layer up like you're climbing Sani Pass.
rows.draft: Apara liaparo tse ngata joalo ka ho palama Sani Pass.
rows.reason: 'Apara diaparo tse ngata' is the phrasing already in the confirmed lines, 'ho palama' suits climbing, and Sani Pass stays as the place name.

rows.en: Everything looks like a film scene. A creepy one.
rows.draft: Tsohle li shebahala joalo ka filimi. E tšosang.
rows.reason: Short and natural; 'filimi e tšosang' echoes the confirmed 'filimi ea tšabo'. 'Scene' is dropped but the creepy-film feel comes through.

rows.en: It is what it is.
rows.draft: Ke seo e leng sona.
rows.reason: 'Ke seo e leng sona' is a word-for-word carry of the English idiom; a speaker would shrug with 'Ho jwalo feela'.
rows.rewrite: Ho jwalo feela.

rows.en: Welkom-cold today. The kind that goes through three jerseys like they aren't there.
rows.draft: Welkom-cold kajeno. Serame se fetang ka di-jersey tse tharo jwalo ka ha di se teng.
rows.reason: 'Welkom-cold' stays as a code-switched place tag like the confirmed Karoo/Pretoria lines, and 'serame' with 'di-jersey tse tharo' reads naturally; the jersey image comes through.

rows.en: The garden's saying dankie at last.
rows.draft: Jarata e re kea leboha qetellong.
rows.reason: 'Jarata' is the word the natives use for the garden, 'e re kea leboha' is a natural way to have the garden speak, and 'qetellong' gives the 'at last'.

rows.en: Nature's having a word. Best to listen.
rows.draft: Tlhaho e batla ho bua. Ho molemo ho mametsa.
rows.reason: 'ho mametsa' is not the infinitive of 'listen'; it is 'ho mamela'. The rest ('Tlhaho e batla ho bua') is fine.
rows.rewrite: Tlhaho e batla ho bua. Ho molemo ho mamela.

rows.en: Maybe rain, maybe not. Classic.
rows.draft: Mohlomong pula, mohlomong che. Setso.
rows.reason: 'Mohlomong pula, mohlomong che' is how a speaker would say it, and 'Setso' is the word natives already used for 'Classic'.

rows.en: Sun's out. Don't be fooled. Nature is lying.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le tjhabile. O se ke wa thetswa. Nature e bua leshano.
rows.reason: 'Nature' is left in English where Sesotho has 'tlhaho' (used in the confirmed lines); the rest of the line works.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le tjhabile. O se ke wa thetswa. Tlhaho e bua leshano.

rows.en: The dog is still keen. The dog is always keen. Respect.
rows.draft: Ntja e ntse e le keen. Ntja e dula e le keen. Respect.
rows.reason: 'keen' (twice) and 'Respect' are raw English doing all the work; a speaker would say what the dog wants and use 'Hlompha' as the natives did for 'respect'.
rows.rewrite: Ntja e ntse e batla ho tsamaya. Ntja e lula e batla ho tsamaya. Hlompha.

rows.en: Trust issues with the sky today.
rows.draft: Mathata a tšepo le lehodimo kajeno.
rows.reason: 'Mathata a tšepo le lehodimo' is a calque of 'trust issues'; a speaker would say they have trouble trusting the sky.
rows.rewrite: Ke na le mathata a ho tšepa lehodimo kajeno.

rows.en: Bottle this one. Open it in winter.
rows.draft: Beha lena ka botlolong. Bula nakong ea mariha.
rows.reason: Clear, warm and complete in Sesotho: 'beha lena ka botlolong' and 'bula nakong ea mariha' carry the bottle-it-for-winter idea without strain.

rows.en: You will look like a lobster. You've been warned.
rows.draft: O tla shebahala joalo ka lobster. O lemoselitsoe.
rows.reason: Lobster stays as a loan like steak and pool, the sunburn warning is plain and dry; 'o lemoselitsoe' is slightly stiff but understood.

rows.en: Looks wet. The models are fairly sure, not certain.
rows.draft: Ho bonahala ho le metsi. Limodele li na le bonnete mohlomong, eseng ka botlalo.
rows.reason: 'bonnete mohlomong' ('certainty maybe') is a stiff translated phrase for 'fairly sure'; 'eseng ka botlalo' also reads heavy.
rows.rewrite: Ho bonahala ho le metsi. Limodele li batla li na le bonnete, empa ha li na tiisetso.

rows.en: The UV index is higher than your expectations.
rows.draft: UV index e phahameng ho feta litšepo tsa hao.
rows.reason: 'e phahameng ho feta' uses the relative form where the sentence needs 'e phahame ho feta' (the natives fixed the same pattern in the sunscreen-budget line), and 'litšepo' means hopes or promises, not expectations.
rows.rewrite: UV index e phahame ho feta seo u se lebelletseng.

rows.en: The fridge is the coolest room in the house.
rows.draft: Fridge ke kamore e pholileng ka ho fetisisa ka tlung.
rows.reason: 'ka tlung' is off: the natives write 'ka ntlong' for in the house. Fridge stays as the loan, like heater.
rows.rewrite: Fridge ke kamore e pholileng ka ho fetisisa ka ntlong.

rows.en: Your hairstyle? Gone. Accept it.
rows.draft: Moriri oa hao? O ile. Amohela.
rows.reason: Short, dry and natural: 'Moriri oa hao? O ile. Amohela.' keeps the deadpan of the English.

rows.en: The braai cover is in the next suburb.
rows.draft: Sekoahelo sa braai se seterekeng se latelang.
rows.reason: 'setereke' means a district, not a suburb; a speaker would say 'sebaka' (the natives used streets for the same joke).
rows.rewrite: Sekwahelo sa braai se sebakeng se latelang.

rows.en: The kids still going to school in shorts. They know things we don't.
rows.draft: Bana ba ntse ba ya school ka shorts. Ba tseba dintho tseo rona re sa di tsebeng.
rows.reason: 'school' is left raw where Sesotho has 'sekolo' (as with 'huddled' and 'farmer' that the natives replaced); the rest is natural.
rows.rewrite: Bana ba ntse ba ya sekolong ka shorts. Ba tseba dintho tseo rona re sa di tsebeng.

rows.en: Cancel everything. Even your excuses.
rows.draft: Hlakola tsohle. Esita le mabaka a hao.
rows.reason: 'Hlakola' for cancel and 'esita le mabaka a hao' both match the natives' own usage; the turn on 'even your excuses' lands.

rows.en: Water consumption: yes. All of it.
rows.draft: Ho noa metsi: e. Kaofela.
rows.reason: Stiff form-field calque: 'Ho noa metsi: e.' reads as a translated checklist; a speaker would ask the question and answer it.
rows.rewrite: Ho noa metsi? E. Kaofela.

rows.en: Postcard weather. You're welcome.
rows.draft: Leholimo la postcard. Kea leboha.
rows.reason: 'Kea leboha' means 'thank you', the opposite of 'you're welcome', so the brag turns into a thank-you; 'U amohelehile' is the usual 'you're welcome'.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo la postcard. U amohelehile.

rows.en: Somewhere a roof is someone's new kite.
rows.draft: Mohlomong sebakeng se seng marulelo ke khaete e ncha.
rows.reason: 'Mohlomong' (maybe) wrongly hedges the English 'somewhere', 'someone's' is missing, and the natives' word for 'somewhere' is 'kae-kae'.
rows.rewrite: Kae-kae lerulelo ke khaete e ncha ea motho.

rows.en: Cape Town just got a dimmer switch.
rows.draft: Cape Town e fumane konopo ea ho fokotsa lesedi.
rows.reason: 'Konopo ea ho fokotsa lesedi' explains a dimmer switch in a long stiff phrase; people just say the loan, as with wiper and out-of-office.
rows.rewrite: Cape Town e sa tswa fumana dimmer switch.

rows.en: Maybe rain, maybe not. Classic.
rows.draft: Mohlomong pula, mohlomong che. Tloaelo.
rows.reason: Short and dry like the kept 'Mohlomong pula'; 'Tloaelo' carries the 'typical' tone (che is only the older spelling of tjhe).

rows.en: Lightning's putting Eskom's grid to shame.
rows.draft: Lehadima le hlabisa Eskom dihlong.
rows.reason: 'Hlabisa Eskom dihlong' is a natural put-to-shame idiom and carries the lightning-beats-the-grid joke.

rows.en: Somewhere between fine and soaked. Good luck.
rows.draft: Pakeng tsa ho loka le ho ba metsi. Katleho.
rows.reason: Clear and natural; 'metsi' for wet is the natives' word and 'Katleho' matches the kept 'Good luck out there'; 'soaked' is a little weaker but the meaning lands.

rows.en: Might spit a bit. Might not bother.
rows.draft: Ho ka tšela hanyane. Ho ka se tshoenyehe.
rows.reason: 'Tshoenyehe' means troubled or worried, not 'can't be bothered' (the natives use 'khathala'), and 'tšela' means pour, not spit a little.
rows.rewrite: Ho ka na hanyane. Ho ka se khathale.

rows.en: Good soup weather, not gonna lie.
rows.draft: Leholimo le letle la soupa.
rows.reason: 'Soupa' is the banned loan, the word is 'sopho'; the dry 'not gonna lie' tag is dropped.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le lokileng la sopho, ka nnete.

rows.en: The clouds RSVP'd 'maybe' and showed up anyway.
rows.draft: Maru a arabile 'mohlomong' empa a fihlile.
rows.reason: 'A arabile mohlomong empa a fihlile' is natural and the maybe-then-arrived turn works even without the RSVP word.

rows.en: Coffee in the sun on the stoep. The whole reason we live here.
rows.draft: Coffee letsatsing stoepong. Ke lona lebaka lohle leo re dulang mona.
rows.reason: Raw 'Coffee' where the natives always write 'kofi' (they changed it in the kettle line); the rest reads naturally.
rows.rewrite: Kofi letsatsing stoepong. Ke lona lebaka lohle leo re dulang mona.

rows.en: Not the time for hero moves, hey.
rows.draft: Ha se nako ea bosenatla, hey.
rows.reason: Uses 'Ha se nako ea ...' the way the kept 'Ha se taba e kgolo' does; I cannot fully vouch for 'bosenatla' for hero moves, but it reads plausibly and 'hey' is ordinary SA code-switching.

rows.en: Perfect excuse to cancel plans.
rows.draft: Lebaka le letle la ho hlakola merero.
rows.reason: 'Hlakola merero' is the natives' own verb for cancelling plans and 'lebaka' matches their 'excuse'; plain, warm and natural.

rows.en: The bins are on an adventure again.
rows.draft: Matlakala a tsamaisong hape.
rows.reason: 'Tsamaisong' means in the management/procedure, not on an adventure, and 'matlakala' is rubbish rather than bins, so a reader would not get the joke.
rows.rewrite: Dibini tsa matlakala di leetong hape.

rows.en: Probably a bit of cloud. Or a lot. Hard to call.
rows.draft: Mohlomong ho na le maru a manyane. Kapa a mangata. Ho thata ho bolela.
rows.reason: Built from the natives' own 'ho na le maru' and 'maru a manyane'; 'Ho thata ho bolela' is a natural way to say hard to call.

rows.en: The sky's giving mixed signals again.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le fana le matšoao a tsoakaneng hape.
rows.reason: 'Fana le' as in the kept 'Lehodimo le fana le tsohle' and 'matšoao a tsoakaneng' for mixed signals is natural and clear.

rows.en: Eskom wishes it had this power.
rows.draft: Eskom e ka rata matla ana.
rows.reason: 'Matla' carries both strength and electrical power, so the Eskom pun survives; short and natural.

rows.en: Not depressing. Just... underwhelming.
rows.draft: Ha ho masoabi. Feela... ha ho khotsofatse.
rows.reason: Understandable and natural in tone ('ha ho masoabi' is a little loose for depressing, but it reads fine); the deflating turn lands.

rows.en: Cape Town's twinkling. Probably.
rows.draft: Cape Town e phatsima. Mohlomong.
rows.reason: 'E phatsima' suits twinkling city lights and the dry 'Mohlomong' tag matches the kept hedged lines.

rows.en: Your makeup has an expiry date of 9am.
rows.draft: Grimase ea hao e na le nako ea ho fela ea 9 hoseng.
rows.reason: 'Grimase' is not a word I can place for makeup (not in the app's corpus); people say the loan 'make-up'. Rest of the line is fine.
rows.rewrite: Make-up ea hao e na le nako ea ho fela ka 9 hoseng.

rows.en: Looks warm. How warm is a moving target.
rows.draft: Ho bonahala ho futhumetse. Hore na ho futhumetse hakae ho a fetoha.
rows.reason: The second sentence is stiff ('Hore na ... hakae ho a fetoha') and loses the moving-target image; a speaker would put a comma after the 'how warm' clause.
rows.rewrite: Ho bonahala ho futhumetse. Hore ho futhumetse hakae, ho ntse ho fetoha.

rows.en: Even the weather apps are arguing about this one.
rows.draft: Esita le di-app tsa leholimo li phehisana ka sena.
rows.reason: 'Esita le' and the hyphenated loan 'di-app' are in the natives' register; 'phehisana' is their word for arguing.

rows.en: The fridge door is getting a workout today.
rows.draft: Monyako oa fridge o fumana boikoetliso kajeno.
rows.reason: Keeps 'fridge' as a loan like the natives do (heater, duvet); 'boikoetliso' for workout reads naturally and the joke carries.

rows.en: Probably hot. We'll all find out together.
rows.draft: Mohlomong ho chesa. Re tla fumana kaofela hammoho.
rows.reason: Plain, dry and understandable; 'Re tla fumana kaofela hammoho' keeps the shared-suspense turn. Only the older 'chesa' spelling, which is not a fault by itself.

rows.en: Could be worse. Could also be better.
rows.draft: E ka ba mpe le ho feta. E ka ba betere le ho feta.
rows.reason: Two flat parallel beats, like the English; 'mpe' and the 'betere' loan are ordinary speech. 'Le ho feta' on both halves leans slightly toward 'even better' but the shrug still comes through.

rows.en: Cloud cover with a side of who-cares.
rows.draft: Maru le lehlakore la mang ea tsotellang.
rows.reason: 'Maru le lehlakore la ...' is a word-for-word 'with a side of': lehlakore means a side/flank, not a side dish, and 'maru le' does not read as 'cloud cover with'. The shrug of 'mang ea tsotellang' is fine but the spine of the line is a calque.
rows.rewrite: Maru a koahetse lehodimo, mme ha ho motho ya tsotellang.

rows.en: The hadedas are sleeping. Finally.
rows.draft: Dinonyana di robetse. Qetellong.
rows.reason: 'Dinonyana di robetse. Qetellong.' is natural and the dry 'Finally' works; birds for hadedas matches the confirmed 'Esita le dinonyana di kgutsitse'. The hadeda specificity is lost but the relief still reads.

rows.en: Solidarity to everyone with one wet shoe right now.
rows.draft: Kopano le bohle ba nang le seeta se le seng se metsi joale.
rows.reason: 'Kopano le bohle ...' is 'unity with everyone', a slogan word that sounds stiff and translated for a joke about one wet shoe; a speaker would say 'we are with everyone who ...'. 'Joale' is the older spelling.
rows.rewrite: Re mmoho le bohle ba nang le seeta se le seng se metsi hona jwale.

rows.en: The sky is buffering.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le a buffera.
rows.reason: Same loan-plus-Sesotho-verb pattern as the confirmed 'le sa loadhella'; short, dry and lands for anyone who has watched a spinner.

rows.en: Hot water bottle is the real MVP today.
rows.draft: Botlolo ea metsi a chesang ke mohale oa 'nete kajeno.
rows.reason: 'Botlolo ea metsi a chesang' is a plain name for the hot water bottle and 'mohale oa nnete' is a warm way to say the real MVP; reads like something a person would say.

rows.en: The sky's undecided. So are we.
rows.draft: Leholimo ha le qeta. Le rona.
rows.reason: 'Ha le qeta' means 'it does not finish'; 'undecided' needs 'etsa qeto' (make a decision), as in the confirmed 'Lehodimo ha le e-s'o etse qeto'. 'Le rona' then has nothing to hang on.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo ha le e-s'o etse qeto. Le rona.

rows.en: Not a hairstyle in sight. Just survivors.
rows.draft: Ha ho setaele sa moriri se bonahalang. Ba pholosehileng feela.
rows.reason: 'Ba pholosehileng' means those who were saved or rescued (it sounds religious); 'survivors' is 'ba pholohileng'. The first half is natural.
rows.rewrite: Ha ho setaele sa moriri se bonahalang. Ba pholohileng feela.

rows.en: Thunder so close the walls shook. Respect.
rows.draft: Modumo o haufi mabota a thothomela. Hlompho.
rows.reason: Telegraphic: 'Modumo o haufi mabota a thothomela' strings two clauses with no 'so close that', and the English past ('shook') becomes present. Needs 'hoo' to connect them.
rows.rewrite: Modumo o ne o le haufi hoo mabota a thothomelang. Hlompho.

rows.en: Outside is a test of character. You're failing.
rows.draft: Kantle ke teko ea botho. O a hloleha.
rows.reason: 'Botho' is humanity or decency (ubuntu), not 'character' in the toughness sense, so 'a test of botho' reads as a moral test; 'boitšoaro', which the natives use for 'attitude', is closer. 'O a hloleha' is a good punch.
rows.rewrite: Kantle ke teko ea boitšoaro. O a hloleha.

rows.en: Even the seagulls are walking today.
rows.draft: Esita le dikoekoe di tsamaea kajeno.
rows.reason: 'Dikoekoe' is not a seagull word I can vouch for, and bare 'di tsamaea' is just 'go/leave'; the point is that they walk instead of flying, which needs 'ka maoto'. Safer to use a plain phrase for sea birds.
rows.rewrite: Esita le dinonyana tsa lewatle di tsamaya ka maoto kajeno.

rows.en: Shoes optional. Attitude mandatory.
rows.draft: Lieta li ka khethoa. Boitšoaro bo tlamehile.
rows.reason: 'Li ka khethoa' is 'can be chosen', not 'optional'; the confirmed line uses 'ke kgetho' for 'not optional'. 'Boitšoaro' for attitude is right, and 'lieta' should be 'dieta'.
rows.rewrite: Dieta ke kgetho. Boitšoaro bo tlamehile.

rows.en: Flip-flops on tar was a mistake.
rows.draft: Lislipase ho tara e ne e le phoso.
rows.reason: 'Lislipase' is a garbled noun that a speaker would not recognise (the plural is also in the older li- form); and with a plural subject the 'e ne e le' agreement is off. People just say the loan: 'E ne e le phoso ho apara flip-flops ...'.
rows.rewrite: E ne e le phoso ho apara flip-flops holim'a tara.

rows.en: Probably windy. The Cape Doctor keeps its own diary.
rows.draft: Mohlomong ho na le moea. Cape Doctor e na le bukana ea eona.
rows.reason: 'Bukana' is a small book or booklet, not a diary or schedule, so 'keeps its own diary' is a calque; the confirmed corpus uses 'lenaneo' for a schedule. The natives also turned the Cape Doctor into 'Ngaka ea Cape'.
rows.rewrite: Mohlomong ho na le moya. Ngaka ya Cape e na le lenaneo la yona.

rows.en: Storm on the cards, not yet confirmed. Stay sharp.
rows.draft: Sefefo se monyetleng, ha se e-s'o netefatsoe. Lula u falimehile.
rows.reason: The first half is right and matches the confirmed 'monyetleng' and 'ha e-s'o netefatse' lines, but 'falimehile' means astonished or dazed, not alert; the confirmed lines use 'Dula u hlokometse'.
rows.rewrite: Sefefo se monyetleng, ha se e-s'o netefatsoe. Dula u hlokometse.

rows.en: Your future self will thank you for that sunscreen.
rows.draft: Uena oa hosane o tla leboha ka setofo sa letsatsi.
rows.reason: 'Setofo' reads as a stove, not sunscreen (a banned word the natives already fixed to 'setlolo sa letsatsi'), so the line now says your future self will thank you for a stove.
rows.rewrite: Uena wa hosane o tla leboha ka setlolo sa letsatsi.

rows.en: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is the worst.
rows.draft: Hobaneng uena-oa-nakong-e-fetileng o entse merero? Uena-oa-nakong-e-fetileng o mobe.
rows.reason: 'Uena-oa-nakong-e-fetileng' is a hyphenated English 'past-you' that no speaker would say, twice over. 'Wena wa maobane' (yesterday's you) carries the idea in everyday speech.
rows.rewrite: Hobaneng o entse merero? Wena wa maobane o mobe ka ho fetisisa.

rows.en: This is the weather the weekend was invented for.
rows.draft: Lena ke leholimo phomolo e entsoeng bakeng sa lona.
rows.reason: 'Phomolo' is rest or holiday, not the weekend (the corpus uses 'mafelo a beke'), and 'leholimo phomolo e entsoeng' drops the relative 'leo', so it reads as translated word for word.
rows.rewrite: Lena ke lehodimo leo mafelo a beke a entsweng bakeng sa lona.

rows.en: Don't trust those clouds. They're plotting.
rows.draft: Se ke oa tšepa maru ao. A rera.
rows.reason: 'Se ke oa tšepa maru ao' is natural and 'A rera' (they are planning) is as dry and short as the English. A native might want 'a a rera' or an object, but it stands.

rows.en: Schrodinger's rain. It both is and isn't.
rows.draft: Pula ea Schrödinger. E teng le ha e eo.
rows.reason: 'Pula ea Schrödinger' is good, but 'le ha' means 'although/even if', so 'E teng le ha e eo' reads 'it is there even though it isn't'; 'mme' gives the 'both ... and'.
rows.rewrite: Pula ya Schrödinger. E teng, mme ha e eo.

rows.en: Save this one in the memory bank.
rows.draft: Boloka letsatsi lena mohopolong.
rows.reason: Warm and natural; 'boloka ... mohopolong' is the ordinary way to say keep this in your memory, even though the bank image is dropped.

rows.en: Somewhere a cricket is really giving it.
rows.draft: Kae-kae tšie e binela ka matla.
rows.reason: 'Tšie' (tsie) is a grasshopper; the cricket that chirps is 'tswiritswiri' (a known error in this app). 'Kae-kae' and the rest are right.
rows.rewrite: Kae-kae tswiritswiri e bina ka matla.

rows.en: Your vitamin D levels are thanking you.
rows.draft: Maemo a hao a vitamin D a a leboha.
rows.reason: "maemo" means conditions or circumstances, not levels, and "a a leboha" lacks the object (thanking you); a speaker would say the vitamin D itself is thanking you.
rows.rewrite: Vitamin D ea hao e a o leboha.

rows.en: Ja, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.
rows.draft: E, ke leholimo la jersey. Jersey tse peli.
rows.reason: Natural code-switched "jersey" (as in the Bloemfontein line natives kept); the double-jersey turn carries over.

rows.en: The sun's on airplane mode.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le ho airplane mode.
rows.reason: "Letsatsi le ho airplane mode" follows the same pattern as the confirmed "Di-wiper di ho max"; the loan phrase is what people say and the personified sun lands.

rows.en: The dog's under the bed. Smart move, honestly.
rows.draft: Ntja e ka tlas'a bethe. Mohato o bohlale, ka nnete.
rows.reason: Plain, warm and natural; "ka nnete" and the dog-as-sensible-character turn match the confirmed dog lines.

rows.en: The ice cream van is playing everyone's anthem.
rows.draft: Bane ea ice cream e bapala pina ea bohle.
rows.reason: "Bane" reads as a misspelt "bana" (children), not "van"; and music is played with "letsa", not "bapala". A speaker would say "koloi ea ice cream".
rows.rewrite: Koloi ea ice cream e letsa pina ea bohle.

rows.en: The office aircon debate just went to level 5.
rows.draft: Puisano ea aircon ea ofisi e sa tsoa fihla boemong ba 5.
rows.reason: "Puisano" (a calm discussion) is too polite for an office aircon fight, which is a "khang"; "boemong ba 5" is stiff where people just say "level 5".
rows.rewrite: Khang ea aircon ofising e sa tsoa fihla level 5.

rows.en: The fog arrived unannounced. Classic fog.
rows.draft: Moholi o fihlile a sa memioa. Moholi oa setso.
rows.reason: "a sa memioa" means uninvited, not unannounced, and the participial "a" does not agree with "moholi" (class 3). A speaker would say it came without notice.
rows.rewrite: Mohodi o fihlile ntle le tsebiso. Mohodi oa setso.

rows.en: Dark outside, bright tomorrow.
rows.draft: Ho fifala kantle, ho phatsima hosane.
rows.reason: Short, rhythmic and warm; "ho fifala ... ho phatsima hosane" carries the same hopeful turn.

rows.en: Walking into it feels like a video game boss fight.
rows.draft: Ho tsamaea ho eona ho ikutloa joalo ka ntoa ea boss ea papali ea video.
rows.reason: Stiff and translated throughout: "ho tsamaea ho eona" has no antecedent for "eona", and "ntoa ea boss ea papali ea video" is clumsy. A speaker would say walking outside feels like fighting a boss in a video game.
rows.rewrite: Ho tsamaya kantle ho ikutloa eka ke ho loana le boss ea video game.

rows.en: The sky's reminding us who's boss.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le re hopotsa hore ke mang monga'a.
rows.reason: "monga'a" is an unfinished possessive (owner of ...), not "boss"; a speaker would say who is in charge, "ea laolang".
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le re hopotsa hore ke mang ea laolang.

rows.en: No filter needed. Just look outside.
rows.draft: Ha ho hlokahale filitha. Sheba kantle feela.
rows.reason: Natural, with a clean "ha ho hlokahale ... Sheba kantle feela" turn; the adapted loan "filitha" is understood, though the loan left as "filter" would also pass.

rows.en: Ice cream isn't a treat. It's survival.
rows.draft: Ice cream ha se mpho. Ke bophelo.
rows.reason: "mpho" means a gift, not a treat, and "ke bophelo" reads as "it's life" rather than survival; the word for survive is "pholoha".
rows.rewrite: Ice cream ha se feela ntho e monate. Ke ho pholoha.

rows.en: Hot-ish, likely. Keep the water close.
rows.draft: Ho chesa mohlomong. Boloka metsi haufi.
rows.reason: Plain, natural and practical; "mohlomong" carries the hedge and "boloka metsi haufi" is how a speaker would say it.

rows.en: The weekend doesn't get better than this.
rows.draft: Phomolo ha e be betere ho feta mona.
rows.reason: "Phomolo" means rest, not weekend (the confirmed word is "mafelo a beke"), and "ho feta mona" is stiff for "better than this".
rows.rewrite: Ha ho mafelo a beke a betere ho feta sena.

rows.en: Rain so heavy it should pay rent.
rows.draft: Pula e boima haholo e lokela ho lefa rente.
rows.reason: Reads naturally and the rain-as-a-tenant joke lands intact; the "rente" loan is what people say.

rows.en: Bring a jacket. Or don't. We're only fairly sure.
rows.draft: Nka baki. Kapa che. Re na le bonnete feela mohlomong.
rows.reason: "baki" is not jacket (the word is "jase"), and "re na le bonnete feela mohlomong" reads as "only certainty, maybe" instead of "only fairly sure".
rows.rewrite: Tlisa jase. Kapa tjhe. Re na le bonnete ba hoo e ka bang.

rows.en: Highveld winter: the only place where you wear two jackets to fetch the post.
rows.draft: Highveld winter: ke moo o aparang jackets tse pedi ho lata post.
rows.reason: "jackets" and "post" are left raw where Sesotho has "dijase" and "poso", "winter" is mariha, and "ke moo" loses the "only place" force.
rows.rewrite: Mariha a Highveld: ke moo feela o aparang dijase tse pedi ho ea lata poso.

rows.en: Your shoes are about to have a bad day.
rows.draft: Lieta tsa hao li tla ba le letsatsi le lebe.
rows.reason: Natural; the shoes with a bad day personified keep the dry understatement of the English.

rows.en: No alarm. No agenda. Just vibes.
rows.draft: Ha ho alarm. Ha ho agenda. Vibes feela.
rows.reason: Sesotho grammar ("ha ho ...") around natural urban loans; "vibes feela" matches the confirmed "vibes feela" line.

rows.en: Somewhere a chocolate bar just died.
rows.draft: Mohlomong sebakeng se seng tšokolate e sa tsoa qhibiliha.
rows.reason: The added "mohlomong" (maybe) undoes the "somewhere ... just died" certainty; the confirmed word for "somewhere" is "kae-kae". "Died" becoming "melted" is acceptable.
rows.rewrite: Kae-kae tšokolate e sa tsoa qhibiliha.

rows.en: Wind's on the cards. Peg the washing down.
rows.draft: Moea o monyetleng. Hokahanya liaparo tsa ho hlatsoa.
rows.reason: "Hokahanya" means to connect or arrange, and "liaparo tsa ho hlatsoa" is clothes waiting to be washed, not washing on the line; the second sentence says something else. The first sentence is fine.
rows.rewrite: Moya o monyetleng. Tiisa diaparo tse fanyehileng.

rows.en: Walking the dog has become a trust exercise.
rows.draft: Ho tsamaisa ntja e fetohile papali ea tšepo.
rows.reason: "e fetohile" agrees with "ntja" (the dog) instead of the infinitive subject "ho tsamaisa"; "ho tsamaya le ntja" is the natural way to say walking the dog.
rows.rewrite: Ho tsamaya le ntja ho fetohile papali ea tšepo.

rows.en: Whoever has a pool today is your new best friend.
rows.draft: Mang kapa mang ea nang le pool kajeno ke motsoalle oa hao e mocha e moholo.
rows.reason: Natural; 'motswalle oa hao e moholo' is the same best-friend phrasing natives kept for the heater line, and the pool-as-friend turn carries.

rows.en: Hold onto your hat! And your kids.
rows.draft: Tšoara katiba ea hao! Le bana ba hao.
rows.reason: Short, plain and natural; 'Tšoara' is used the same way in a kept line, and the dry second beat 'Le bana ba hao' lands.

rows.en: Pack an umbrella. Or don't. We don't know either.
rows.draft: Paka sekhele. Kapa o se ke oa paka. Ha re tsebe le rona.
rows.reason: Natural; 'sekhele' is the natives' umbrella word, the negative imperative is correct, and 'Ha re tsebe le rona' keeps the shrug.

rows.en: Visibility sponsored by nobody.
rows.draft: Ho boneha ho sponsoritsoe ke motho. Motho.
rows.reason: 'ke motho' means 'by a person', not 'by nobody' (that is 'ha ho motho'), so the line says the opposite; the dangling 'Motho.' and the forced 'sponsoritsoe' make it unreadable.
rows.rewrite: Ho boneha: ha ho motho ea e lefellang.

rows.en: Breezy, probably. Maybe more.
rows.draft: Ho foka hanyane, mohlomong. Mohlomong ho feta.
rows.reason: Natural hedge; 'Ho foka hanyane, mohlomong' reads like speech and 'Mohlomong ho feta' keeps the 'maybe more' beat, if a little clipped.

rows.en: Walking to the bin is now an expedition.
rows.draft: Ho tsamaea ho ea bining joale ke leeto.
rows.reason: Natural code-switched 'bining' and clear; 'leeto' is a plain trip, so the 'expedition' size is slightly softer but the joke still comes through.

rows.en: Night looks calm. Models permitting.
rows.draft: Bosiu bo bonahala bo khutsitse. Haeba limodele li lumela.
rows.reason: Natural; 'limodele' is the word natives kept, and 'Haeba limodele li lumela' carries the dry 'models permitting'.

rows.en: Warm enough to leave the window open. Brave enough?
rows.draft: Ho futhumetse ho lekane ho bula fensetere. O sebete?
rows.reason: Natural question-turn; 'O sebete?' echoes the 'o ikutlwa o le sebete' wording natives kept, and 'ho futhumetse ho lekane' is idiomatic.

rows.en: Sky's throwing rocks. Stay inside.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le lahla majoe. Sala ka hare.
rows.reason: Natural and vivid; 'Sala ka hare' is the natives' own phrase for stay inside, and 'lahla majoe' (throw stones) gets across hail.

rows.en: Even your phone's overheating.
rows.draft: Esita le mohala oa hao o chesang.
rows.reason: Not a full sentence: 'mohala oa hao o chesang' is only 'your phone that is hot', with no verb for 'is overheating'.
rows.rewrite: Esita le mohala oa hao o a tjhesa.

rows.en: The kind of day you text someone about.
rows.draft: Mofuta oa letsatsi oo o romelang motho molaetsa ka lona.
rows.reason: Natural; 'Mofuta oa letsatsi' follows a kept native line, and 'romela motho molaetsa' is correct for texting someone; reads warm.

rows.en: Braai weather, boet! No excuses.
rows.draft: Leholimo la braai, boet! Ha ho mabaka.
rows.reason: A speaker could have written it: 'Leholimo la braai' matches the kept 'lehodimo la ...' pattern and 'Ha ho mabaka' is a kept native phrase; 'boet' stays.

rows.en: Blue sky, warm breeze. The simple stuff.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le letala, moea o futhumetseng. Lintho tse bonolo.
rows.reason: 'letala' means green; blue sky is 'leputsoa'. The rest ('moea o futhumetseng', 'Lintho tse bonolo') is fine.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le leputsoa, moya o futhumetseng. Lintho tse bonolo.

rows.en: The office aircon war has begun.
rows.draft: Ntoa ea aircon ea ofisi e qalile.
rows.reason: Natural code-switch: 'aircon' and 'ofisi' stay as people say them, 'Ntoa ea ... e qalile' is a clean, funny war announcement.

rows.en: You could fry an egg on the N1.
rows.draft: O ka chesa lehe ho N1.
rows.reason: 'chesa lehe' is 'burn/heat an egg', not cook or fry one; natives used 'besa' for cooking a steak on the pavement, and 'ho N1' is stiff for 'on the N1'.
rows.rewrite: O ka besa lehe holim'a N1.

rows.en: Rooibos consumption just doubled.
rows.draft: Tšebeliso ea rooibos e sa tsoa phethahala habeli.
rows.reason: Stiff and translated: 'Tšebeliso ea rooibos' (use of rooibos) is formal, and 'phethahala' means be completed; a speaker would say that drinking rooibos increased.
rows.rewrite: Ho noa rooibos ho sa tswa eketseha habeli.

rows.en: Rain on the way, give or take.
rows.draft: Pula e tla, mohlomong.
rows.reason: Natural short hedge; 'Pula e tla, mohlomong' is what a speaker would say, only the 'give or take' shade is thin.

rows.en: Even the geyser is putting in extra hours.
rows.draft: Esita le geyser e sebetsa lihora tse eketsehileng.
rows.reason: Natural; 'Esita le geyser' keeps the loan, and 'e sebetsa ... tse eketsehileng' matches the kept overtime line for the ponytail holders.

rows.en: Even the parking lot looks pretty today.
rows.draft: Esita le sebaka sa liphakinki se bonahala se setle kajeno.
rows.reason: 'sebaka sa liphakinki' is a forced, pluralised loan that sounds stiff; people just say 'parking', and 'shebahala' is the natives' word for looks.
rows.rewrite: Esita le parking e shebahala e le ntle kajeno.

rows.en: Your hands are in your pockets and they're not coming out.
rows.draft: Matsoho a hao a lipokothong 'me ha a tsoe.
rows.reason: Natural and dry; 'a lipokothong' (in pockets) and the negative 'ha a tsoe' give the same stubborn second beat as the English.

rows.en: Storm's possible. The braai might need a rain check.
rows.draft: Sefefo se ka etsahala. Braai e ka hloka letsatsi le leng.
rows.reason: Natural; 'Sefefo se ka etsahala' is plain Sesotho and 'letsatsi le leng' fairly carries 'rain check', though the idiom is softened.

rows.en: Hot chocolate is not a want. It's a need.
rows.draft: Tšokolate e chesang ha se takatso. Ke tlhoko.
rows.reason: Clean parallel: 'ha se takatso. Ke tlhoko.' keeps the want/need turn, and 'tšokolate e chesang' is the natural way to say hot chocolate.

rows.en: Visibility: basically zero.
rows.draft: Ho boneha: hanyenyane nul.
rows.reason: 'hanyenyane nul' is unclear: it mixes 'a tiny bit' with Afrikaans 'nul' and does not say 'basically zero'; natives used 'hoo e ka bang ...' for approximately.
rows.rewrite: Ho boneha: hoo e ka bang zero.

rows.en: The sun doesn't care about your plans.
rows.draft: Letsatsi ha le khathalele merero ea hao.
rows.reason: Mirrors the confirmed fog line 'ha o khathalele lenaneo la hao'; dry, natural, meaning intact.

rows.en: Tan lines are not a personality trait.
rows.draft: Mela ea ho tjhesa ha se botho.
rows.reason: 'Mela ea ho tjhesa' means lines of burning, not tan lines, and 'ha se botho' reads as 'is not humane'; a speaker would just say 'tan lines' and use botho ba hao for personality.
rows.rewrite: Tan lines ha se botho ba hao.

rows.en: Sky's looking moody. Could escalate.
rows.draft: Leholimo le bonahala le halefile. Ho ka eketseha.
rows.reason: 'Ho ka eketseha' (could increase) is a calque of 'escalate'; a speaker would say it could get worse (ho mpefala).
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le bonahala le halefile. Ho ka mpefala.

rows.en: 50/50 on the rain. Bring a jacket, just in case.
rows.draft: 50/50 ka pula. Nka baki, e le ka mohla.
rows.reason: 'E le ka mohla' does not mean 'just in case' and reads oddly; the confirmed corpus says 'jase' for jacket.
rows.rewrite: 50/50 ka pula. Nka jase, ho molemo ho ba le eona.

rows.en: Some wind expected. Strength still TBC.
rows.draft: Ho lebeletsoe moea o itseng. Matla ha a e-s'o netefatsoe.
rows.reason: Dry bulletin register carries the 'TBC' joke; 'ha a e-s'o netefatsoe' matches the kept 'stars haven't confirmed' line (only Lesotho spelling moea/lebeletsoe).

rows.en: The fridge feels warmer than the lounge today.
rows.draft: Fridge e ikutloa e futhumetse ho feta lounge kajeno.
rows.reason: Fridge and lounge as loans are the code-switching natives allow (heater, pool, AC); 'ikutloa e futhumetse' parallels the kept 'maoto a ikutlwa'.

rows.en: The world got a soft filter this morning.
rows.draft: Lefatše le fumane filitha e bonolo hoseng.
rows.reason: 'Filitha' is a forced respelling of filter that a speaker would not write (just 'filter', as with 'vibes'); 'hoseng' alone is 'in the morning', 'hoseng hona' is this morning.
rows.rewrite: Lefatše le fumane filter e bonolo hoseng hona.

rows.en: Today's forecast: medium rare.
rows.draft: Ponelopele ea kajeno: medium rare.
rows.reason: 'Ponelopele' is the confirmed forecast word and 'medium rare' stays as the English steak idiom, like the kept steak lines.

rows.en: The wind has a personal vendetta against umbrellas.
rows.draft: Moea o na le vendetta ea motho ka bo eena khahlanong le disekhele.
rows.reason: 'Vendetta ea motho ka bo eena' is a stiff calque of 'personal vendetta' with a forced Italian loan; a speaker says the wind hates umbrellas, using 'ka bo mong' for personally as in the kept sun line.
rows.rewrite: Moya o hloile disekhele ka bo mong.

rows.en: Forecast: vibes neutral, expectations lower.
rows.draft: Ponelopele: vibes li bohareng, litebello li tlase.
rows.reason: Deadpan 'ponelopele: vibes ... litebello li tlase' keeps the two-beat turn; 'vibes' and 'bohareng' match kept lines.

rows.en: The lapa cushions are crispy.
rows.draft: Di-cushion tsa lapa di crispy.
rows.reason: 'Di-cushion' pluralised like the kept 'Di-koppies' and 'Di-fleece'; the English 'crispy' is the joke and survives as an everyday loan.

rows.en: Probably cold. Take the jersey, you'll thank us.
rows.draft: Mohlomong ho bata. Nka jeresi, u tla re leboha.
rows.reason: Natural 'mohlomong ho bata' plus 'u tla re leboha' lands the friendly nudge; same shape as the kept low-confidence cold lines.

rows.en: Unplug the things. The sky has plans.
rows.draft: Tlosa lintho ho motlakase. Lehodimo le na le merero.
rows.reason: 'Tlosa lintho ho motlakase' is terse but clear and the dry 'lehodimo le na le merero' turn works.

rows.en: Reapply that sunscreen or suffer.
rows.draft: Tšoaea hape kapa o hloke.
rows.reason: 'Tšoaea' is not 'apply', 'sunscreen' is never named, and 'o hloke' means you lack, not you suffer; the line does not say the English.
rows.rewrite: Tlotsa setlolo sa letsatsi hape, kapa o tla utlwa bohloko.

rows.en: Even the shade is sweating.
rows.draft: Esita le moriti o a fufuleloa.
rows.reason: Shade personified like the kept 'moriti o futhumetse' and 'moriti o sebetsa'; the sweating verb is plausible though I cannot fully verify the form.

rows.en: The kind of sky that makes you grateful for free things.
rows.draft: Mofuta oa lehodimo o etsang hore o leboge lintho tsa mahala.
rows.reason: 'Leboge' is the Setswana form (leboga); Sesotho says 'lebohe'. The rest follows the kept 'mofuta oa letsatsi o etsang hore ...' pattern.
rows.rewrite: Mofuta wa lehodimo o etsang hore o lebohe dintho tsa mahala.

rows.en: Sky's grumbling. Stay close to a roof.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le a duma. Lula haufi le marulelo.
rows.reason: 'Lehodimo le a duma' (duma, as in seaduma) is natural and 'haufi le marulelo' echoes the confirmed storm line.

rows.en: The ozone layer called. It's on leave.
rows.draft: Ozone layer e llelitse. E leaveng.
rows.reason: 'E llelitse' means has cried for, not called (letsetsa is the called/phoned verb); 'leaveng' is an English loan with -ng, which natives replaced with matsatsi a phomolo for holiday.
rows.rewrite: Ozone layer e letsetsitse. E matsatsi a phomolo.

rows.en: Jislaaik, stay inside!
rows.draft: Eish, dula ka hare!
rows.reason: 'Eish' for jislaaik is already confirmed (heat line) and 'dula ka hare' is the plain natural command.

rows.en: Sunscreen is not optional, boet.
rows.draft: Setofo sa letsatsi ha se kgetho, boet.
rows.reason: 'Setofo' reads as stove (banned word); sunscreen is 'setlolo sa letsatsi'. Rest ('ha se kgetho, boet') is natural.
rows.rewrite: Setlolo sa letsatsi ha se kgetho, boet.

rows.en: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.
rows.draft: Letamo le ne le tebile ho feta kamoo le neng le shebahala kateng. Le lula le tebile.
rows.reason: 'Le lula le tebile' echoes the kept 'Braai e dula e etsahala'; letamo for a puddle was accepted by a native; a little wordy but natural.

rows.en: This is the stuff. Right here.
rows.draft: Ke sona sena. Mona feela.
rows.reason: 'Ke sona sena' is the everyday 'this is it' exclamation and 'mona feela' closes it warmly.

rows.en: Probably fog later. The Boland does this.
rows.draft: Mohlomong mohodi hamorao. Boland e etsa sena.
rows.reason: SA 'mohodi' and 'Boland e etsa sena' mirror the confirmed cold line; 'hamorao' for later is natural.

rows.en: The sky is the colour of an old Tupperware lid.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le na le 'mala oa sekoahelo sa Tupperware sa khale.
rows.reason: Reads naturally; 'colour of an old lid' carries the grey-sky image and the Tupperware loan lands.

rows.en: Your car seat is a weapon right now.
rows.draft: Setulo sa koloi ea hao ke sebetsa joale.
rows.reason: Uses the same 'sebetsa' (weapon) pattern as the confirmed car-door line; the hot-seat meaning comes through from the heat context.

rows.en: Take a brolly just in case, hey.
rows.draft: Nka sekhele ho ba sireletsehile, hey.
rows.reason: 'ho ba sireletsehile' (to be protected) is a stiff calque of 'just in case'; a speaker would say 'lest it rains'.
rows.rewrite: Nka sekhele, esere pula e na, hey.

rows.en: 50/50 on getting wet. Like a coin toss.
rows.draft: 50/50 ho ba metsi. Joalo ka papadi.
rows.reason: 'Papadi' means a game, not a coin toss, so the second beat loses its image; 'ho ba metsi' is also stiff for getting wet.
rows.rewrite: 50/50 hore pula e o fumane. Jwalo ka ho lahlela chelete.

rows.en: This is the weather we brag about overseas.
rows.draft: Lena ke leholimo leo re le iponelang lichaba.
rows.reason: 're le iponelang lichaba' is garbled and does not say 'brag'; the verb for boasting is 'ho ikgantsha'.
rows.rewrite: Lena ke lehodimo leo re ikgantshang ka lona ka mose ho lewatle.

rows.en: Cloud's the call. With an asterisk.
rows.draft: Maru ke karabo. Ka letšoao.
rows.reason: 'Ka letšoao' (with a sign) does not say 'asterisk', so the caveat joke goes flat; 'ke karabo' is also stiff for 'the call'.
rows.rewrite: Maru ke seo re se behang. Ka asterisk.

rows.en: Even the Capetonians are admitting it's cold.
rows.draft: Esita le ba Cape ba lumela hore ho a bata.
rows.reason: Natural; 'esita le' and 'ho a bata' match confirmed lines and 'lumela hore' reads as 'admit'.

rows.en: Welkom, Sasolburg, Kroonstad: the koue belt is doing its koue thing.
rows.draft: Welkom, Sasolburg, Kroonstad: koue belt e etsa koue thing ya yona.
rows.reason: The koue repetition survives, but 'koue thing ya yona' leaves 'thing' in English; natives replaced the English leftover ('brave face') in the comparable line.
rows.rewrite: Welkom, Sasolburg, Kroonstad: koue belt e etsa ntho ya yona ya koue.

rows.en: Africa's sky just hits different.
rows.draft: Lehodimo la Afrika le fapane feela.
rows.reason: 'Le fapane feela' just means 'is different', neutral to flat; 'hits different' needs the good sense said.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo la Afrika le fapane haholo, ka tsela e ntle.

rows.en: The sun is technically present. Spiritually elsewhere.
rows.draft: Letsatsi ka tsela ea ts'ebetso le teng. Ka moea le sebakeng se seng.
rows.reason: 'ka tsela ea ts'ebetso' means 'by way of operation', not 'technically'; a speaker would keep the loan 'technically'.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le teng, technically. Moya wa lona o kae-kae.

rows.en: Don't touch the seatbelt buckle. Trust us.
rows.draft: Se ke oa ama buckle ea seatbelt. Re tšepe.
rows.reason: Natural; 'Se ke oa ama' and 'Re tšepe' match confirmed phrasing, and the loans buckle and seatbelt stay as people say them.

rows.en: Slip-slops, shorts, sun. The trinity.
rows.draft: Slip-slops, libhulukoe tse khutšoanyane, letsatsi. Boraro bo bong.
rows.reason: 'Boraro bo bong' is the Sesotho word for the Trinity, so the joke lands; slip-slops stays as a loan.

rows.en: Even the bakkies on the N2 pulled over.
rows.draft: Esita le li-bakkie tsa N2 li emile ka thoko.
rows.reason: Natural; 'esita le', the li-bakkie plural and 'li emile ka thoko' (pulled over) all read as speech.

rows.en: Protect that face! It's the only one you've got.
rows.draft: Sireletsa sefahleho seo! Ke se le seng feela o nang le sona.
rows.reason: Plain, warm and dry; 'sireletsa sefahleho' and 'se le seng feela' carry the English exactly.

rows.en: Cloud's around. How much is up for debate.
rows.draft: Maru a potolohile. Hore na a makae ke ngangisano.
rows.reason: 'a potolohile' means 'have gone round', not 'are around'; a speaker would say 'maru a teng' as in the confirmed lines.
rows.rewrite: Maru a teng. Hore ke a makae, ke ngangisano.

rows.en: The sky's giving 'I'll try again tomorrow' energy.
rows.draft: Lehodimo le fana le 'ke tla leka hosane' matla.
rows.reason: 'le fana le ... matla' is a calque of 'giving ... energy'; a speaker would let the sky say the sentence itself.
rows.rewrite: Lehodimo le bonahala le re, 'Ke tla leka hape hosane.'

rows.en: The geyser tripped overnight. Of course it did.
rows.draft: Geyser e tripile bosiu. Of course e entse jwalo.
rows.reason: 'tripile' and the raw English 'Of course' are forced; natives replaced the same kind of Sesotho-ised verb ('startile'), and a speaker would say 'e timile' and 'ehlile'.
rows.rewrite: Geyser e timile bosiu. Ehlile e entse jwalo.

rows.en: Garage pie for lunch because the kitchen is lava.
rows.draft: Paee ea garage hobane kitchen ke lava.
rows.reason: 'Paee ea garage' drops 'for lunch' and who is eating, so it reads as a pie belonging to the garage.
rows.rewrite: Re ja paee ka garage motsheare, hobane kitchen ke lava.

rows.en: Coffee count: rising. Motivation count: still zero.
rows.draft: Palo ea kofi: e nyolohang. Palo ea khothatso: e ntse e le zero.
rows.reason: Natural counting joke; 'palo ea kofi' and 'khothatso' match confirmed wording and 'zero' stays as a loan.

rows.en: Even your GPS is confused.
rows.draft: Esita le GPS ea hao e ferekane.
rows.reason: 'Esita le ... e ferekane' is idiomatic for confused and GPS stays as a loan.

rows.en: Your nose is going to betray you by 3pm.
rows.draft: Nko ea hao e tla o eka ka 3pm.
rows.reason: 'ho eka' for betray matches the confirmed 'Kantle ho u eka' line; '3pm' stays as people type it.

rows.en: The sun's on a tea break. No ETA.
rows.draft: Letsatsi le phomoletseng ho noa tee. Ha ho ETA.
rows.reason: 'le phomoletseng' is a relative clause left hanging as a sentence; a speaker would say the sun has taken a break ('phomotse') to drink tea.
rows.rewrite: Letsatsi le phomotse ho noa tee. Ha ho ETA.

rows.en: The vibe is beige. Accept it.
rows.draft: Vibe ke beige. Amohela.
rows.reason: Short and dry; 'Vibe' and 'beige' stay as loans like the confirmed vibe line, and 'Amohela' is a natural imperative.
